name: DEAP-3600
notes: DEAP-3600 is a single-phase liquid argon SCINTILLATION detector, not a two-phase time projection chamber: it has no drift field and no ionization/charge readout, and detects only scintillation light via its 255 PMTs, using pulse-shape discrimination of that scintillation signal (deap3600.ca; Astropart. Phys. 108 (2019) 1-23, Sec. 1). technology_classes lists 'noble_liquid_tpc'/'argon_tpc' only because the ontology's enum has no separate scintillator-only class, per the dark-matter lead's convention in docs/atlas-worklog/dark-matter.md; this should not be read as DEAP-3600 having TPC-style charge readout.

summary.plain: DEAP-3600 is a dark matter experiment 2 km underground at SNOLAB in Canada. It watches 3.6 tonnes of liquid argon for the faint flash of light a dark matter particle would make hitting an argon nucleus. It has taken data since late 2016 and is currently being upgraded for a further run.
summary.technical: Single-phase liquid argon scintillation detector (no drift field, no ionization/charge readout) at SNOLAB's 2 km level (6000 m.w.e.). Design target of 3600 kg LAr (~3300 kg maintained fill since Nov 2016), 1000 kg fiducial mass within a 55 cm radius, viewed by 255 8-inch Hamamatsu R5912-HQE PMTs. Sets the leading argon-target WIMP-nucleon exclusion limits above ~30 GeV/c2 and searches for superheavy multi-scattering dark matter; currently in a hardware upgrade phase toward a further ('third') fill.
